title: Five Numbers, No New Signs
label: ch:ja-numbers-one-to-five
canDo: I can say and write one to five in Japanese, and I can say which number has a native word standing beside its borrowed reading.

payoff.summary: Run ichi to go in order, then name the two of the five that were already yours and say where you had met each.
payoff.note: JA-A1-NUM-01 was ticked on ONE numeral, and that one was inside a phrase. The chapter opens on ichi and go rather than on ichi and ni because both were already in the reader's hands and neither costs a sign: ichi has been said since chapter 9 inside mou ichido, whose lesson states that ichi is one, and go is the kanji 五, whose chapter-5 script lesson says on the page that the sign means five on its own and then asks for nothing but its sound. yon lands last because the on'yomi/kun'yomi seam is only legible once the run exists.
